definition: Reflective awareness — the I-awareness (ahaṃtā) by which consciousness turns back on itself and knows itself. Lit. 'the act of considering, reflecting, examining.' In Trika, it is the self-awareness of Śiva — the 'I' that knows itself. The dynamic aspect of consciousness that makes self-recognition possible.

sources.claim: vimarśa is the defining characteristic of consciousness — without it, consciousness would be inert (jaḍa)
vimarśa as the self-awareness that constitutes the Lord's nature
Vimarśa = the act of considering, reflecting, examining. In Trika, it is the self-awareness of Śiva.

translations.note: 'Reflective awareness' captures the active, self-turning aspect; 'reflection' is too passive; 'I-awareness' is technical but precise.
